questions.q: The 46XX DSD chapter opens with two broad heads. Which pair heads the tree printed at the top of the page?
opts: Abnormal development of gonads and abnormal karyotype
Abnormal development of gonads and ambiguous genitalia
Abnormal development of gonads and androgen insensitivity
questions.exp: Page 160 splits 46XX DSD into abnormal development of gonads (ovotestes, Turner's syndrome) and ambiguous genitalia (raised maternal androgens, placental aromatase deficiency).

questions.q: Under 'abnormal development of gonads', the two entries listed are:
questions.exp: Abnormal development of gonads has 1. Ovotestes and 2. Turner's syndrome.

questions.q: Fill up: The chapter is titled 'Disorders of sexual development in ____'.
questions.exp: The heading on page 160 is 'Disorders of sexual development in 46XX'.

questions.q: True/False: In the 46XX DSD tree, ovotestes is filed under 'abnormal development of gonads'.
opts: False - it is filed under ambiguous genitalia
False - it is filed under placental aromatase deficiency
questions.exp: Ovotestes is the first entry under abnormal development of gonads.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a branch printed under 'ambiguous genitalia' in the 46XX tree?
questions.exp: Turner's syndrome sits under abnormal development of gonads; the three others are under ambiguous genitalia.

questions.q: A 46XX DSD classification lists 'a. Turner's syndrome' with the sub-line '45 XO (m/c) → streak ovary'. Which additional karyotype is printed under the mosaic arm?
questions.exp: The mosaic entry prints 45XO → streak ovaries and 46XY → dysgenetic testes.

questions.q: Match the Turner's karyotype with the gonad printed beside it - 1) 45XO (m/c) 2) Mosaic 45XO 3) Mosaic 46XY ... A) Streak ovaries B) Dysgenetic testes C) Streak ovary
questions.exp: 45XO (m/c) → streak ovary; mosaic 45XO → streak ovaries; mosaic 46XY → dysgenetic testes.

questions.q: Under raised maternal androgens, the three sources printed are:
opts: Androgen secreting tumour, luteoma and androgenic drugs
Androgen secreting tumour, luteoma and placental aromatase deficiency
Luteoma, androgenic drugs and Turner mosaic
Androgenic drugs, theca lutein cysts and luteoma
questions.exp: Raised maternal androgens lists androgen secreting tumour, luteoma, and androgenic drugs.

questions.q: Which tumour of pregnancy is named as a maternal source of androgens causing 46XX DSD?
questions.exp: Luteoma of pregnancy is listed as an androgen-secreting tumour under raised maternal androgens.

questions.q: Fill up: The third item under ambiguous genitalia in the 46XX tree is placental ____ deficiency.
questions.exp: Placental aromatase deficiency is the third item under ambiguous genitalia.

questions.q: Scenario: A pregnant woman with no history of drug intake delivers a virilised 46XX infant. Imaging shows no maternal tumour. Which listed mechanism best explains the virilisation?
questions.exp: With no tumour and no drugs, the remaining printed cause is placental aromatase deficiency.

questions.q: In placental aromatase deficiency, the arrow printed is 'aromatase ↓ → estrogen ↓'. What else is marked as raised?
questions.exp: The block prints 'aromatase ↓ → estrogen ↓' together with '↑ maternal androgen'.

questions.q: Which statement about the printed 46XX DSD tree is correct?
opts: Turner's syndrome appears under ambiguous genitalia
Placental aromatase deficiency appears under gonadal causes
Luteoma appears under abnormal development of gonads
Turner's syndrome appears under gonadal causes, not under ambiguous genitalia
questions.exp: Only the first statement matches the printed tree.

questions.q: Fill up: Ovotestes carries the old term ____ hermaphrodite.
questions.exp: The page prints 'Old term: True hermaphrodite'.

questions.q: The karyotype frequency in ovotestes is printed as:
questions.exp: Karyotype: 46XX > 46XY.

questions.q: A child with ovotesticular DSD is karyotyped. Which result would the printed order make the MORE likely finding?
questions.exp: Because 46XX exceeds 46XY in ovotestes.

questions.q: Odd one out - which term is NOT a printed synonym or label for ovotestes?
questions.exp: True hermaphrodite is the old term; Turner mosaic belongs to the Turner branch, not ovotestes.

questions.q: True/False: In ovotestes, 46XY is more common than 46XX.
opts: True - they are equal in the printed text
questions.exp: The printed order is 46XX > 46XY, so 46XY is not more common.

questions.q: Which of the following best states why the old label 'true hermaphrodite' was used for ovotestes?
opts: The external genitalia are always female
Both Mullerian and Wolffian ducts persist in every case
Both ovarian and testicular tissue are present in the same individual
questions.exp: The term reflects the presence of both ovarian and testicular tissue.

questions.q: The MOST common pattern of gonadal distribution in ovotestes is:
opts: One ovary and one testis, one on each side
Ovarian plus testicular tissue on both sides
Bilateral ovaries with a unilateral testis
A single gonad containing only testicular tissue
questions.exp: Pattern (a): 1 ovary + 1 testis on each side - marked most common.

questions.q: The LEAST common pattern printed for ovotestes is:
opts: One ovary and one testis on each side
Ovarian and testicular tissue on both sides
Bilateral testes with a unilateral ovary
Unilateral ovotestis with a streak gonad
questions.exp: Pattern (b) - ovarian + testicular tissue on both sides - is marked L/c (least common).

questions.q: Fill up: The internal genitalia in ovotestes show both ____ and ____ internal genitalia.
questions.exp: 'Internal genitalia: Both male + female internal genitalia.'

questions.q: On the side of the ovary, the internal genitalia are:
questions.exp: 'On the side of ovary → Female internal genitalia.'

questions.q: On the side of the testis, the internal genitalia are:
questions.exp: 'On the side of testes → male internal genitalia.'

questions.q: Match the gonadal side with the internal genital duct derivative - 1) Side of ovary 2) Side of testis ... A) Male internal genitalia B) Female internal genitalia
questions.exp: Ovary side gives female internal genitalia; testis side gives male internal genitalia.

questions.q: A surgeon removes a left ovary and finds a Fallopian tube and hemi-uterus on that side. According to the printed rule this is because:
opts: The internal genitalia follow the gonad on that side
AMH from the contralateral testis failed
questions.exp: The rule printed is that internal genitalia correspond to the gonad on the same side.

questions.q: True/False: In ovotestes the internal genitalia are uniformly female regardless of which gonad is present.
opts: True - unless a testis is palpable
True - because AMH is always absent
questions.exp: Both male and female internal genitalia occur, following the gonad on each side.

questions.q: Odd one out - which finding does NOT follow the printed 'side of the gonad' rule?
opts: Fallopian tube on the side of the ovary
Vas deferens on the side of the testis
Bilateral Fallopian tubes with a testis on each side
Hemi-uterus on the side of the ovary
questions.exp: Bilateral tubes with bilateral testes contradicts the rule; the other three follow it.

questions.q: The external genitalia in ovotestes are described as ambiguous AND resembling:
questions.exp: 'Ambiguous resembling male external genitalia d/t testosterone from adrenals.'

questions.q: Fill up: The ambiguous male-like external genitalia in ovotestes are attributed to testosterone from the ____.
questions.exp: Printed: 'd/t testosterone from adrenals'.

questions.q: At birth, a child with ovotestes is MOST commonly presumed to be:
questions.exp: 'm/c presumed as male at birth'.

questions.q: What fraction of ovotesticular cases show gynaecomastia?
questions.exp: Printed: '>= 3/4th cases: Gynaecomastia (+) (d/t estrogen)'.

questions.q: Gynaecomastia in ovotestes is attributed to:
questions.exp: The bracketed cause is '(d/t estrogen)'.

questions.q: What fraction of ovotesticular patients menstruate at puberty?
questions.exp: 'At puberty: 1/4th cases: menstruation (+)'.

questions.q: Match the pubertal event in ovotestes with its printed frequency - 1) Gynaecomastia 2) Menstruation ... A) 1/4th cases B) >= 3/4th cases
questions.exp: Gynaecomastia in >= 3/4th; menstruation in 1/4th.

questions.q: Scenario: A 15-year-old reared male presents with breast enlargement and cyclical bleeding per urethra. Karyotype 46XX. Which ovotesticular statistic pair fits?
opts: Gynaecomastia is rare; menstruation occurs in most
Gynaecomastia is expected in most; menstruation occurs in a minority
questions.exp: Gynaecomastia >= 3/4th and menstruation 1/4th - common first, uncommon second.

questions.q: True/False: The external genitalia in ovotestes are virilised because of testosterone produced by the testicular tissue itself.
opts: True - the testis is the only source named
True - adrenal androgen is explicitly excluded
questions.exp: The page attributes the virilisation to testosterone from the adrenals.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed pubertal feature of ovotestes?
questions.exp: Voice deepening is a 5-alpha reductase deficiency page feature, not printed here.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: Fill up: Pathophysiology of CAH is introduced as the ____ cause of DSD in 46XX.
questions.exp: 'm/c cause of DSD in 46XX'.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: What genital outcome does CAH produce in the 46XX fetus?
questions.exp: 'Ambiguous genitalia in females'.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: Which trophic hormone drives the adrenal cortex in the printed physiology diagram?
questions.exp: ACTH is shown acting on the adrenal gland at the top of the diagram.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: Fill up: The adrenal steroidogenic precursor printed at the head of both pathways is ____.
questions.exp: Pregnenolone is the parent steroid in the diagram.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: Which enzyme converts pregnenolone to progesterone?
questions.exp: 3-beta HSD is printed on the pregnenolone-to-progesterone arrow.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: Which enzyme converts pregnenolone to 17-OH pregnenolone?
questions.exp: 17-alpha hydroxylase acts on pregnenolone to give 17-OH pregnenolone.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: Fill up: 17-OH pregnenolone is converted to DHEA by ____.
questions.exp: The 17,20 lyase step generates DHEA.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: DHEA is converted to androstenedione by which enzyme?
questions.exp: The side box prints 'DHEA --3beta HSD--> Androstenedione'.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: Which androgen is labelled the 'stronger androgen' in the printed summary?
questions.exp: 'DHEA → Androstenedione → Testosterone (Stronger androgen)'.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: In females, the printed fate of testosterone is conversion by aromatase into:
questions.exp: 'In females aromatase → Estrogen'.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: Which two adrenal end-products carry the printed phrase 'negative feedback on ACTH'?
questions.exp: Both aldosterone and cortisol branches show negative feedback on ACTH.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: Match the mineralocorticoid pathway - 1) Progesterone to deoxycorticosterone 2) Deoxycorticosterone to corticosterone 3) Corticosterone to aldosterone ... A) 11-beta hydroxylase B) aldosterone synthase C) 21-alpha hydroxylase
questions.exp: 21-alpha hydroxylase, then 11-beta hydroxylase, then aldosterone synthase.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: Match the glucocorticoid pathway - 1) 17-OH progesterone to 11-deoxycortisol 2) 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol ... A) 11-beta hydroxylase B) 21-alpha hydroxylase
questions.exp: 21-alpha hydroxylase then 11-beta hydroxylase.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: Which pair of enzymes is printed as the adrenal gland's list on the sex-steroid side?
questions.exp: The right-hand list prints 1. 17-alpha hydroxylase, 2. 17,20 lyase.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: Which triplet of enzymes is printed on the adrenal gland's corticosteroid side?
questions.exp: The left-hand list prints 1. 21-alpha hydroxylase, 2. 11-beta hydroxylase, 3. 3-beta HSD.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: Fill up: Two distinct estrogen products are printed as estradiol and ____ from aromatase action.
questions.exp: The diagram prints 'Estrogen (E2)' and 'Estrogen (E1)'.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: Scenario: A block is placed at 3-beta HSD. Which three adrenal products all fall together?
questions.exp: 3-beta HSD sits before the mineralocorticoid, glucocorticoid and androgen arms, so all three end-products drop.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: True/False: In the printed diagram, aromatase acts on androstenedione and testosterone to give estrogens.
opts: False - aromatase only acts on testosterone
False - aromatase converts DHEA to androstenedione
questions.exp: Aromatase arrows are shown from both androstenedione and testosterone to estrogen.

questions.unit: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map
questions.q: Odd one out - which enzyme is NOT part of the printed adrenal steroidogenic map?
questions.exp: 5-alpha reductase is a peripheral conversion enzyme, not in this adrenal map.

questions.q: Fill up: Hyponatraemia in CAH is listed under the consequences of deficient ____.
questions.exp: Hyponatraemia is grouped under 'D/t ↓ aldosterone'.

questions.q: Which electrolyte rises in CAH because aldosterone is deficient?
questions.exp: Hyperkalaemia is listed under decreased aldosterone.

questions.q: The phrase 'salt water wasting' is printed with which accompanying descriptor?
questions.exp: 'Salt water wasting (dehydration)'.

questions.q: Which acid-base disturbance is listed under aldosterone deficiency in CAH?
questions.exp: Metabolic acidosis is printed in the aldosterone-deficiency group.

questions.q: Hypoglycaemia in CAH is a consequence of deficient:
questions.exp: Hypoglycaemia is grouped under 'D/t ↓ cortisol'.

questions.q: Match the metabolic derangement with its deficient hormone - 1) Hypoglycaemia 2) Hyperkalaemia 3) Metabolic acidosis ... A) Aldosterone B) Cortisol
questions.exp: Cortisol deficiency gives hypoglycaemia; aldosterone deficiency gives hyperkalaemia and metabolic acidosis.

questions.q: Odd one out - which feature belongs to cortisol deficiency rather than aldosterone deficiency?
questions.exp: Hypoglycaemia is the sole cortisol-deficiency item; the other three are aldosterone-deficiency items.

questions.q: Fill up: Loss of negative feedback in CAH raises ACTH, which in turn raises androgens and ____.
questions.exp: 'D/t loss of negative feedback: ↑ ACTH → ↑ Androgens, 17-OH progesterone ↑'.

questions.q: As a consequence of raised androgens, the female fetus shows and the male fetus shows:
opts: Normal external genitalia; normal external genitalia
questions.exp: Females: ambiguous genitalia. Males: normal external genitalia.

questions.q: True/False: The newborn male with CAH has ambiguous genitalia according to this page.
questions.exp: Males have normal external genitalia; only females are ambiguous.

questions.q: Scenario: A 2-week-old 46XX infant presents with vomiting, dehydration, hyperkalaemia and ambiguous genitalia. Which mechanism explains BOTH the electrolyte and the genital findings?
opts: Aldosterone deficiency plus loss of negative feedback raising androgens
questions.exp: One mechanism (enzyme block) produces aldosterone deficiency and, via lost feedback, androgen excess.

questions.q: Which of the four listed aldosterone-deficiency features is printed with a bracketed explanation?
questions.exp: Only 'salt water wasting' carries the bracket '(dehydration)'.

questions.q: Fill up: The screening test for CAH is serum ____.
questions.exp: '1. Screening test: 17-OH progesterone'.

questions.q: A screening 17-OH progesterone below 200 ng means:
questions.exp: '<200 ng → Rule out CAH'.

questions.q: A screening value at or above 800 ng means:
questions.exp: '>= 800 ng → Confirm CAH'.

questions.q: Which screening band mandates the ACTH stimulation test?
questions.exp: '200-800 ng → Diagnostic test: ACTH stimulation test'.

questions.q: Fill up: The diagnostic test named for the intermediate 17-OH progesterone band is the ____ test.
questions.exp: ACTH stimulation test is printed as the diagnostic test.

questions.q: Match the 17-OH progesterone value with the action - 1) <200 ng 2) 200-800 ng 3) >=800 ng ... A) ACTH stimulation test B) Rule out CAH C) Confirm CAH
questions.exp: Below 200 rules out; 200-800 needs stimulation; 800 and above confirms.

questions.q: Scenario: A neonate with ambiguous genitalia has a screening 17-OH progesterone of 540 ng/dL. What is the correct next step per the printed algorithm?
questions.exp: 540 falls in the 200-800 band, which routes to the ACTH stimulation test.

questions.q: True/False: Treatment must wait for karyotyping before it is started.
opts: True - treatment starts only after the ACTH test
questions.exp: Printed: 'Treatment started without waiting for karyotyping results, based on physical examination findings'.

questions.q: Which physical-examination finding makes ambiguous genitalia a medical emergency here?
questions.exp: 'Ambiguous genitalia + No palpable gonads → Treated as medical emergency'.

questions.q: Fill up: The drug of choice for the emergency management of CAH is ____.
questions.exp: '1. DOC: Glucocorticoids'.

questions.q: The second drug class in the emergency list is:
questions.exp: '2. Mineralocorticoids'.

questions.q: The fourth step in emergency management is:
questions.exp: '4. Correction surgery for clitoromegaly later'.

questions.q: Match the emergency steps with their order - 1) First 2) Second 3) Third 4) Fourth ... A) Mineralocorticoids B) Correct electrolyte imbalance C) Glucocorticoids D) Surgery for clitoromegaly later
questions.exp: The printed order is glucocorticoids, mineralocorticoids, correct electrolytes, later surgery.

questions.q: Which four investigations are listed under 'send for investigation later'?
opts: 17-OH progesterone, serum electrolytes, glucose and karyotyping/FISH
Serum electrolytes, glucose, LH and FSH
questions.exp: The deferred list is 17-OH progesterone, serum electrolytes, glucose, karyotyping/FISH.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT in the deferred investigation list?
questions.exp: ACTH stimulation is the diagnostic test in the earlier algorithm, not in the deferred list.

questions.q: Scenario: A neonate with ambiguous genitalia and impalpable gonads is brought in dehydrated with hyperkalaemia. Which step must precede the reconstructive surgery?
questions.exp: Surgery for clitoromegaly is listed later; correction of electrolytes is step 3.

questions.unit: Prenatal Dexamethasone and Chorionic Villus Sampling
questions.q: Fill up: The drug of choice named for antenatal suppression is the glucocorticoid ____.
questions.exp: 'DOC: Glucocorticoids - Dexamethasone'.

questions.unit: Prenatal Dexamethasone and Chorionic Villus Sampling
questions.q: Antenatal dexamethasone is started at which gestational age?
questions.exp: 'Started at 4-5 wks of pregnancy'.

questions.unit: Prenatal Dexamethasone and Chorionic Villus Sampling
questions.q: The maximum delay permitted for starting antenatal dexamethasone is:
questions.exp: The bracketed note prints '(maximum delay 9 wks)'.

questions.unit: Prenatal Dexamethasone and Chorionic Villus Sampling
questions.q: Fill up: Chorionic villus sampling for sex determination and gene testing is performed at ____ weeks.
questions.exp: CVS is printed at 10-11 weeks.

questions.unit: Prenatal Dexamethasone and Chorionic Villus Sampling
questions.q: The indication printed at the head of the antenatal algorithm is:
questions.exp: The flow begins with 'Previous child with CAH'.

questions.unit: Prenatal Dexamethasone and Chorionic Villus Sampling
questions.q: If CVS shows a male fetus, the printed instruction is to:
questions.exp: 'male fetus / unaffected female fetus → Discontinue dexamethasone'.

questions.unit: Prenatal Dexamethasone and Chorionic Villus Sampling
questions.q: If CVS shows an affected female fetus, dexamethasone is:
opts: Given only in the third trimester
questions.exp: 'Affected female fetus → Continue dexamethasone'.

questions.unit: Prenatal Dexamethasone and Chorionic Villus Sampling
questions.q: Match the CVS result with the instruction - 1) Male fetus 2) Unaffected female fetus 3) Affected female fetus ... A) Continue dexamethasone B) Discontinue dexamethasone
questions.exp: Only the affected female fetus continues; male and unaffected female stop.

questions.unit: Prenatal Dexamethasone and Chorionic Villus Sampling
questions.q: True/False: The note on this page describes CAH as an X-linked recessive disorder.
opts: False - it is described as autosomal dominant
questions.exp: Printed verbatim: 'Note: CAH: X-linked recessive disorder' (a source quirk - CAH is autosomal recessive in reality).

questions.unit: Prenatal Dexamethasone and Chorionic Villus Sampling
questions.q: Scenario: A woman whose first child had CAH presents at 6 weeks of gestation. What is the correct printed plan?
opts: Wait until 10 weeks to start dexamethasone
Start dexamethasone now and perform CVS at 10-11 weeks
Perform CVS first and start dexamethasone only if the fetus is female
Start dexamethasone only after amniocentesis at 16 weeks
questions.exp: Start at 4-5 weeks (6 is within the 9-week maximum delay) and test by CVS at 10-11 weeks.

questions.unit: Prenatal Dexamethasone and Chorionic Villus Sampling
questions.q: Odd one out - which does NOT appear in the antenatal dexamethasone page?
questions.exp: Amniocentesis is not printed; CVS is the sampling method named.

questions.q: Which enzyme deficiency block opens with the phrase 'Leads to DSD in XY individuals'?
questions.exp: The 17-alpha hydroxylase / 17,20 lyase block carries that line.

questions.q: Fill up: In 17-alpha hydroxylase / 17,20 lyase deficiency the three steroids marked as decreased are DHEA, androstenedione and ____.
questions.exp: The arrows read ↓DHEA, ↓Androstenedione, ↓Testosterone.

questions.q: In 17-alpha hydroxylase / 17,20 lyase deficiency, the female fetus has:
questions.exp: Female fetus: normal external genitalia; male fetus: ambiguous genitalia.

questions.q: In 17-alpha hydroxylase / 17,20 lyase deficiency, the male fetus has ambiguous genitalia because of:
questions.exp: 'male fetus: D/t ↓ Testosterone'.

questions.q: Fill up: In 3-beta HSD deficiency the weak androgen that accumulates is ____.
questions.exp: Printed: '↑ DHEA (weak androgen)'.

questions.q: In 3-beta HSD deficiency, ambiguous genitalia occur in:
questions.exp: The block prints 'Ambiguous genitalia - males + females'.

questions.q: In 3-beta HSD deficiency, virilisation of the female fetus is attributed to:
questions.exp: 'Female fetus: D/t ↑ DHEA'.

questions.q: Which two steroids are printed as deficient in 3-beta HSD deficiency?
questions.exp: The block marks ↓Aldosterone and ↓Cortisol, alongside ↑DHEA and ↓Testosterone.

questions.q: Match the fetal genital outcome to the mechanism - 1) 3-beta HSD deficiency, female fetus 2) 3-beta HSD deficiency, male fetus 3) 17-alpha hydroxylase deficiency, female fetus ... A) D/t decreased testosterone B) Normal external genitalia C) D/t increased DHEA
questions.exp: 3-beta HSD: female virilised by DHEA, male undervirilised by low testosterone; 17-alpha hydroxylase: female normal.

questions.q: Which deficiency is described as a 'newly diagnosed form of CAH'?
questions.exp: P450 OR deficiency is introduced as a newly diagnosed form of CAH.

questions.q: Fill up: P450 is described as an electron ____ for many enzymes.
questions.exp: 'P450: Electron donor for many enzymes'.

questions.q: The skeletal syndrome printed with P450 oxidoreductase deficiency is:
questions.exp: Antley-Bixler syndrome is named beside P450 OR deficiency.

questions.q: The example of skeletal abnormality printed under Antley-Bixler syndrome is:
questions.exp: 'Skeletal abnormalities (Eg: craniosynostosis)'.

questions.q: True/False: P450 oxidoreductase deficiency produces ambiguous genitalia in females only.
opts: True - it spares the male fetus entirely
True - it causes no genital ambiguity at all
questions.exp: It is filed under 'male + females' in the summary.

questions.q: Scenario: A newborn has ambiguous genitalia and craniosynostosis. Which enzyme block links both findings?
questions.exp: P450 OR deficiency is the block printed with Antley-Bixler skeletal abnormalities.

questions.q: Odd one out - which enzyme block is NOT printed with a fetal-sex genital table on this page?
questions.exp: The 21-alpha hydroxylase fetal table is on the CAH page; the 'other causes' page covers the other three.

questions.unit: Summary of Ambiguous Genitalia by Enzyme Defect
questions.q: Fill up: In the summary table, the most common enzyme causing ambiguous genitalia is ____ hydroxylase.
questions.exp: 21-alpha hydroxylase is marked (m/c).

questions.unit: Summary of Ambiguous Genitalia by Enzyme Defect
questions.q: The two enzyme defects filed under 'female only' ambiguous genitalia are:
questions.exp: The female-only column lists 21-alpha hydroxylase (m/c) and 11-beta hydroxylase.

questions.unit: Summary of Ambiguous Genitalia by Enzyme Defect
questions.q: The two defects filed under 'male only' are:
questions.exp: The male-only column lists 17-alpha hydroxylase and 17,20 lyase.

questions.unit: Summary of Ambiguous Genitalia by Enzyme Defect
questions.q: The two defects filed under 'male + females' are:
questions.exp: The combined column lists 3-beta HSD and P450 OR.

questions.unit: Summary of Ambiguous Genitalia by Enzyme Defect
questions.q: Match each defect with its summary column - 1) 11-beta hydroxylase 2) 17,20 lyase 3) P450 OR ... A) Male + females B) Female only C) Male only
questions.exp: 11-beta is female only; 17,20 lyase is male only; P450 OR affects both.

questions.unit: Summary of Ambiguous Genitalia by Enzyme Defect
questions.q: True/False: 21-alpha hydroxylase deficiency appears in the summary under ambiguous genitalia in males only.
opts: True - it spares the female fetus
True - it is listed under male + females
questions.exp: It heads the female-only column and is marked most common.

questions.unit: Summary of Ambiguous Genitalia by Enzyme Defect
questions.q: Which single word marks 21-alpha hydroxylase in the summary?
questions.exp: Printed as '21-alpha hydroxylase (m/c)'.

questions.unit: Summary of Ambiguous Genitalia by Enzyme Defect
questions.q: Odd one out - which defect is NOT filed under 'female only'?
questions.exp: 17-alpha hydroxylase is in the male-only column.

questions.unit: Summary of Ambiguous Genitalia by Enzyme Defect
questions.q: Scenario: A 46XX newborn has ambiguous genitalia and a salt-wasting crisis. Which defect best fits the 'female only, most common' entry?
questions.exp: 21-alpha hydroxylase is the female-only most common defect and matches the CAH salt-wasting picture earlier in the chapter.

questions.unit: Summary of Ambiguous Genitalia by Enzyme Defect
questions.q: Which summary heading covers enzyme defects that virilise the female fetus while undervirilising the male fetus?
questions.exp: 3-beta HSD and P450 OR are grouped under 'male + females'.

questions.q: Fill up: In the 46XX tree, Turner's syndrome is the ____ numbered entry under abnormal development of gonads.
questions.exp: Ovotestes is 1 and Turner's syndrome is 2.

questions.q: Which two sub-lines are printed beneath Turner's syndrome in the tree?
opts: 45XO (m/c) giving streak ovary, and a mosaic arm
45XO giving dysgenetic testis, and a 47XXY arm
46XY giving streak ovaries, and a 45XO arm
questions.exp: The tree prints 45XO (m/c) → streak ovary plus the mosaic sub-branch.

questions.q: Fill up: In the mosaic arm, 45XO gives streak ovaries while 46XY gives ____ testes.
questions.exp: Printed: '46XY: dysgenetic testes'.

questions.q: In the 46XX ambiguous-genitalia arm, which item is numbered 'a'?
questions.exp: 'a. ↑ maternal androgens' heads the ambiguous-genitalia arm.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT printed as a source of raised maternal androgens?
questions.exp: Placental aromatase deficiency is a separate numbered item, not a maternal androgen source.

questions.q: Which karyotype is printed as MOST common in the Turner's branch of the 46XX tree?
True/False: The 46XX chapter lists androgen insensitivity syndrome among its causes.
opts: True - it is listed under ambiguous genitalia
True - it is the second gonadal cause
questions.exp: AIS belongs to the 46XY chapter; the 46XX tree lists ovotestes, Turner's, maternal androgens and aromatase deficiency.

questions.q: Scenario: A virilised 46XX newborn's mother took danazol in early pregnancy. Which printed item covers this?
questions.exp: Androgenic drugs is one of the three listed maternal androgen sources.

questions.q: Match each ovotesticular feature with its descriptor - 1) Old term 2) Karyotype order 3) Commonest pattern 4) Side of testis ... A) 46XX > 46XY B) Ovary on one side, testis on the other C) True hermaphrodite D) Male internal genitalia
questions.exp: Old term true hermaphrodite; 46XX > 46XY; one ovary and one testis on each side; testis side gives male internal genitalia.

questions.q: Which single pubertal feature is explicitly bracketed as being due to estrogen?
questions.exp: 'Gynaecomastia (+) (d/t estrogen)'.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: Fill up: The diagram's topmost regulator, ACTH, is shown acting on the ____.
questions.exp: ACTH is drawn pointing at the adrenal gland.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: In the printed diagram, 17-OH progesterone is the substrate for which enzyme on the cortisol route?
questions.exp: 17-OH progesterone → 11-deoxycortisol via 21-alpha hydroxylase.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: Fill up: 11-deoxycortisol is converted to cortisol by ____ hydroxylase.
questions.exp: The final glucocorticoid step is 11-beta hydroxylase.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: Which enzyme is printed on the progesterone-to-deoxycorticosterone arrow?
questions.exp: 21-alpha hydroxylase converts progesterone to deoxycorticosterone.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: True/False: According to the printed map, DHEA is a weaker androgen than testosterone.
opts: False - DHEA is described as the stronger androgen
questions.exp: DHEA is labelled a weak androgen and testosterone the stronger androgen.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: Which estrogen label is printed on the aromatase arrow from androstenedione rather than from testosterone?
questions.exp: Androstenedione aromatises to E1; testosterone aromatises to E2.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: Odd one out - which steroid is NOT an end-product of the printed adrenal map?
questions.exp: DHT requires peripheral 5-alpha reductase and is not in this adrenal map.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: Scenario: A 46XX neonate has ambiguous genitalia, hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia and hypoglycaemia. Which single enzyme block explains all of these?
questions.exp: 3-beta HSD deficiency lowers aldosterone (hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia), lowers cortisol (hypoglycaemia) and virilises the female fetus via DHEA.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: Which of the five named enzyme blocks is marked as most common?
questions.exp: 21-alpha hydroxylase carries the (m/c) tag in the summary.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: Fill up: The summary table's three column heads are female only, male only and male ____ females.
questions.exp: The third column is headed 'male + females'.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: Match the 17-OH progesterone band with its interpretation - 1) Less than 200 ng 2) 200 to 800 ng 3) 800 ng or more ... A) Confirm CAH B) ACTH stimulation test C) Rule out CAH
questions.exp: Below 200 rules out; the middle band goes to stimulation testing; 800 and above confirms.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: Which drug class is named second in the emergency list, after glucocorticoids?
questions.exp: Step 2 is mineralocorticoids.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: Why is the neonate with ambiguous genitalia and impalpable gonads labelled a medical emergency?
opts: They have an intra-abdominal testis at high malignant risk
They require urgent karyotyping before feeds
They are presumed to have CAH with a salt-wasting crisis
questions.exp: The gonads-not-palpable arm routes to CAH and emergency glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: Fill up: Antenatal dexamethasone is continued only when CVS shows an affected ____ fetus.
questions.exp: 'Affected female fetus → Continue dexamethasone'.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: Which sampling window makes CVS usable before the maximum dexamethasone delay lapses?
opts: 10 to 11 weeks, just after the 9-week maximum delay
questions.exp: Dexamethasone must start by 9 weeks and CVS is done at 10-11 weeks.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: True/False: 3-beta HSD deficiency causes ambiguous genitalia exclusively in 46XX fetuses.
opts: True - it is filed under female only
questions.exp: It is filed under 'male + females'.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: Odd one out - which enzyme block is paired with a named skeletal syndrome?
questions.exp: Only P450 OR deficiency is printed with Antley-Bixler syndrome.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: Scenario: A 46XY newborn has ambiguous genitalia; the 46XX sibling is entirely normal. Which defect fits the printed 'male only' column?
questions.exp: The male-only column lists 17-alpha hydroxylase and 17,20 lyase deficiency.

questions.unit: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass
questions.q: Which enzyme block explicitly prints the phrase 'Leads to DSD in XY individuals'?
questions.exp: That sentence heads the 17-alpha hydroxylase / 17,20 lyase block.
